utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning. Ms. Gopalan.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. The next witness is Mr. Ndrec Konaj.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Would you please read aloud the affirmation which is shown to you now.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Please sit down.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Now Ms. Gopalan has some questions for you.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Konaj.

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Could you please state your full name for the record.

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My name is Ndrec Konaj.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: And what is your date of birth?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: I was born on the 8th of October, 1954.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Mr. Konaj, where do you live now?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: Now I live in Peje, Street UCK, number 149.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you. And what is your occupation, Mr. Konaj?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: I am a building technician.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Konaj, did you provide a statement to the Office of the Prosecutor on the 12th of June, 2001?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Have you recently had the opportunity to review this statement?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: And having reviewed your statement, are you satisfied that the information contained in the statement is true and accurate to the best of your knowledge and belief?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: To the best of my knowledge, it's true. There might be some minor changes due to the way you express your sentences, but in fact it's true in general.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, I seek to tender the witness's statement. It's 65 ter 2372.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: And that will be assigned P00670, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Mr. Konaj, did you testify in the trial of Prosecutor versus Milutinovic et al. in October 2006?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Have you recently had the opportunity to review your testimony in that case?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: And having reviewed your testimony, I understand that you wished to make some changes to it. I will read out the most substantial change that you wished to make and ask that you confirm that the change is correct.

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: At page 4889, line 14, of your testimony you were asked to describe the colours of some vehicles that you saw. The question was: "Q. Can you please describe the one that you identified as a military Pinzgauer, what colour was it?" You answered then: "A. Blue." I understand that you would like to clarify that you had misunderstood the question and that you thought you were being asked about the police Pinzgauer, which was in fact blue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Gopalan --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's correct. There were two Pinzgauers, one military, one police. So that's why there is this misunderstanding regarding the colour because a police Pinzgauer was a blue colour with big tires. It was the same -- the military one was the same but maybe I didn't know how to say -- to express the right word for it. But in general we referred to them as Pinzgauer without making any distinction.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I object to this manner of correcting the transcript, that is, alleged correcting of the transcript. I don't mind the witness saying whatever in answer to the questions of the Prosecution, but this way of correcting the transcript after so many years and after the Prosecution did this in the Milutinovic trial and continuing in this trial, I really object, because this is not a correction of the transcript, this is a new answer at a new trial, and it can affect the cross-examination and my questions. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The concern of the Chamber, Ms. Gopalan, may be the same as that of Mr. Djurdjic or it may be different. I'm not entirely sure. If the witness says that there is something that he finds incorrect in the statement, it would be better if you allowed him to say what it is that he sees to be wrong and what he now wishes to say, rather than you repeat what you may have been told at some earlier time by him. And -- now, I suspect that that is the point Mr. Djurdjic was concerned about as well. So no leading, in effect, upon changes to previous testimony.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Perhaps I could then rephrase the question --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: But we've got the answer now. I think you move on.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Okay. Do I have permission at this point to tender the testimony into evidence, Your Honours?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: If you're ready to do that, yes, it will be received.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Mr. Konaj --

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: It is 05050, 5050 is its 65 ter number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be assigned P00671, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: I'll now read out the witness's in-court summary. The witness is a Kosovo Albanian resident of Pec. In 1999 he was a building inspector. The witness will describe events in Pec on the 27th and 28th of March, 1999, which led to the expulsion of Kosovo Albanians by Serb forces. On the 27th of March, 1999, the witness was staying at his father's house in the Karagaq district of Pec town with his family and some others. In the afternoon, a group of paramilitaries entered his father's yard, shot at the house, and gave the occupants five minutes to leave in the direction of Montenegro. The witness and his family did as instructed and started walking through the streets of Pec. The witness's group was stopped several times, and on one occasion they were stopped by a group of nine men in civilian cars. The witness was assaulted as was his uncle, who was hit in the back with a rifle-butt. On the 28th of March, 1999, the witness and his family were expelled from Pec. En route, the witness saw military, police, and paramilitary troops at every junction to prevent deviation from the route. They were later stopped by a mixed group of Serb forces, who then asked them to return to the town centre where there were thousands of people. About 20 trucks and buses were filled with these displaced persons and driven off in the direction of Prizren. Later that night, the witness go onto a bus with his family. As the convoy travelled south, they were stopped at a check-point opposite the police station in Djakovica. There, the witness saw members of the police and paramilitaries beating a group of men. The bus travelled on towards Prizren, and at the junction to Verbica they were told to leave the bus and walk to Albania. Soon after, other buses appeared and the witness got on one which dropped him off at the border crossing. The witness and his family then walked to the border, where they were told to throw their identification documents into a large box. The witness crossed into Albania on the morning of the 29th of March, 1999. That's the end of the in-court summary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I was too quick, Ms. Gopalan, earlier. We have the witness's explanation for his change. What he hasn't told us is what colour was the Pinzgauer that he was describing. He said it was not the blue one, which was police, but he has not describes the colour of the military one. So you may wish to explore that.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: I believe that's already addressed in the Milutinovic transcript. It's the lines that follow --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: If you're happy with that, okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Mr. Konaj, I have some questions for you. As you know, the Chamber already has before it your statement and testimony in the Milutinovic case, so I have some very specific questions. Let's begin with the events on the 27th of March, 1999. On this day, you were at your father's house, in a neighbourhood in Pec, with your immediate family, some relatives, and others. For the record, this is page 3 of the statement in English. You say that in the afternoon, masked Serbian paramilitary troops entered the neighbourhood and 15 of them entered your father's yard fully armed. Mr. Konaj, what did these paramilitaries say to you and the others who were present at the house?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: They ordered us to leave the house in five minutes and walk in the direction of Montenegro.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you. In paragraph 4 of your statement you say that you and your family walked to the stone bridge, and there you were stopped by two paramilitary soldiers who came from the cafe Stari Most. These two paramilitary soldiers that you mentioned, did you recognise them?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: By sight, yes, but not by name. I didn't know where they lived. I knew them by sight. They were familiar faces.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: And why were they familiar faces to you?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: I had seen them passing by in the streets of the town, but I didn't know who they were. I didn't know their names.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you. You then continued walking, and in the cafe Iliriana, you came across another group of seven policemen. And after that - this is at paragraph 7 of the English - you say that two private cars stopped and nine men got out. Could you tell us what these men did?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: At this stone bridge, as I said, the soldiers stopped us. They separated me and my uncle and put us against the wall, and then our family members started crying. They asked us how much money we had. I said I had 150 Deutschemark. My uncle said he had 10 dinars. And he said, Why do you have so little money on you? I had more because I was the head of the family. That's why I had more money. Then there was a large number of other families expelled from their homes. They told us to leave. When we came to Iliriana, there were these seven policemen. Seven I'm saying; maybe I'm not exact in their number. One of them was dressed in the police uniform. He said to us, You shouldn't walk on the main road. Walk by the side-streets. That's why we started walking by -- on the side-streets.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Konaj. Now, let's take you to when your family was stopped by these two private cars, and you speak about nine men getting out of the cars. What did these men do?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: That's why I was saying. Two cars came by speedily, and they stopped, and they got out of these cars. They ordered me, as I said, and my family to walk in the direction of Montenegro. They said, You have asked Clinton to come, so he should come and rescue you. And they cursed our mothers. They didn't spare any curses. One of them hit me on my chin, another one hit my uncle with a rifle-butt. Then someone from the second car shouted in Serbian: Go to -- let them go, and then we walked in the direction of the bus stop.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Konaj. On that day - this is the 27th of March - you say that you saw groups of Romas and police, that they were drinking together, and that they were breaking into shops and stealing goods. This is at the top of page 4 of the English statement. Where did you see this, Mr. Konaj, in which part of Pec?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: When we left the house of Salih Dreshaj, because we went there on the 27th of March - after they told us to go to Montenegro - there are a couple of stores there. There were group of Roma who entered these stores and stole goods. We saw them stealing goods and drinking beer.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Was --

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: We were taken to the centre.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Was there anyone else with these groups of Roma? Did you see anyone else?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: In every street or side-street on the 28th of March, that is, on the next day, even on the 27th, in every street or side-street, there were two, three, in the main streets, seven, eight policemen, military men, dressed in blue uniforms; and they told us where to go.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: And when you say that you saw goods being stolen, could you tell us what sort of goods these were?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: That's true. I saw them coming out of the store, of the pharmacy with -- loaded with medicaments.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: And do you remember how big this group was?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: You ran into them every 5, 10 metres, all along the way, on both sides of the street.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Do you remember how many people there were in this group that were taking medication or medicaments out of the pharmacy?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: I can't give you an exact figure. It was not a large group, but two, three people, I would say, came out of this pharmacy along -- or along -- from other stores along the way until we went to the centre.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Konaj, I'd now like to move on to the events on the 28th of March. For the record, this is in paragraph 4 of page 4 of the English. You say that on that day you saw crowds of people in the street. They had been evicted from the area of the Catholic church. Mr. Konaj, how do you know that these people had been evicted from the area of the Catholic church?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: At 8.00 in the morning, together with the son of my best man, we left the house and we saw the crowd coming through the side-street. We asked them what happened, and they said that they were evicted from their homes and ordered to go in the direction of Montenegro. And my -- I asked my mother and my mother-in-law to get to the car of my best man; and my wife and my two daughters joined the crowd of people. And all of us, with my uncle, his wife, we walked in the direction of Montenegro. At the school of economics, they stopped us and said, Go back to the centre.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, before we move on to what happened at the school of economics, these people who told you that they had been ordered to go in the direction of Montenegro, did they tell you who had ordered them to head in that direction?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: The police, the army, the paramilitaries, we couldn't tell who exactly, but they -- of course, the same persons who ordered us or who expelled us from our home.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Konaj. Now, you say that at the school of economics they stopped you and asked you to go back to the centre. What did you see in the centre when you headed back there?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: As I already said, on the way from SUP in the direction of the main street, and in that area that I mentioned with these stores, when we went to the centre from Hotel Metohija, Hotel Korsa, all over, was full of people, people evicted from their homes and sent to the centre. In the middle there were lorries, trucks covered, refrigerator trucks, buses, aid trucks, and so on where people got onto; and they were sent in the direction of Albania.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, Mr. Konaj, you say that your family got on one of these vehicles at about 10.00, so later that night you got on a bus with your family. When you got on the bus, did you know where you were going?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: I want to make an explanation. My uncle and my wife got on this truck with a tarpaulin. I asked them to come back, and we went to the last bus together with my daughters, two daughters. The soldier came and asked my friend Bekim Kurti to give him money. He gave him 40 Deutschemark, and he allowed him and my first cousin to enter the bus. I wanted to give that man money, but he didn't ask me for that. So we were nine persons that went into this bus; but when they opened the doors people rushed in, about maybe 100 of them, and they sent us in the direction of Albania.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you. And you also say in your statement - this is English page 5, paragraph 2 - you were stopped at a check-point or the bus was stopped at a check-point in Gjakova opposite the police station. What was happening in that area? What could you see from the bus?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: I was the last in the bus from our group. Ahead of us there was a covered truck. They stopped us at the police station in Gjakove. There were policemen there. They were dressed in camouflage uniforms. I recognised one of them, Miki Stojanovic, nickname Lapoc. He said that all the men should come down, but the driver who was a military man, he didn't allow any one of us to get off the bus. And he said to this man, I have orders to take all of them to Prizren. The other guy that I mentioned said, Okay, when we come back we'll see about that. So we continued on our way in the direction of Prizren.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: We got off the bus at the entrance to Prizren.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: And you say in your statement that you were stopped in Prizren at the junction that leads to Vermice. This is in paragraph 4, page 5, of the English. Could you tell us what the driver of the bus told you at that junction?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: When they left us there he said, This is the road to Albania. Go straight to Albania. Then they said, This is not your country. This is Serbia. Go to your own country, to Albania.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you. And, Mr. Konaj, you say that after that you were picked up by another bus and you arrived at the border at approximately 5.00 a.m. Can you tell us what you witnessed at the border?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: I wanted to add something. When we were told to go to Albania, first one bus came from the direction of Prizren, then another three, and then another two. They told us to walk in the direction -- in that direction, but we didn't. We wanted to get on a second bus. We -- I didn't want to join the convoy with my daughters. I was scared that something might happen to them, so we continued by bus to Vermice, and another military person said to us, Please, just stick to the main road. Don't walk on the side roads because the area is mined. So we continued from Vermice and walked for 7 kilometres. When we arrived at the border, there were policemen there, there were also people dressed in military uniforms, and there was a big wooden box. We were told to throw our identification cards, passports, driver's licences there, registration plates. I pretended that I was throwing my ID card there, but I didn't throw it, in fact, and I have it to this day.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Konaj. Now, I would like to move on to your return to Pec. When was it you returned to Pec, if you recall?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: I don't know the exact day. It was a problem for us to get back. It was impossible to get back when we wanted. When the NATO forces entered Kosova, personally I wanted to go in right away, but I couldn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: When you did return to Pec, do you recall the condition of the buildings in Pec town?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: In the centre of the town and Peje in general, there was a lot of damage caused. The picture was horrific.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: And when you speak of damage caused, could you tell us what sort of damage it is that you saw?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: The houses were burnt down, destroyed; they were razed to the ground.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: And what was the condition of your father's house, if you remember?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: When I went to see my father's house, it was completely demolished in the inside. From the outside it was a little bit burned. There was a fig tree in the yard that caught the fire and the part of the house near the fig tree. The house of my uncle, which is in the same courtyard, was burnt completely.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Konaj. At this stage I have no further questions for you.

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, before I sit down, perhaps I should ask the witness to confirm that apart from the corrections that he made that the transcript is true and accurate to the best of his knowledge and belief. I believe that step was skipped when I was tendering the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: If you believe it was skipped, deal with it.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Mr. Konaj, before I sit down, I'd like to take you back to the questions I had about your transcript. We made some corrections to the transcript which we read out in court. Now, having made those corrections, if you were asked the same questions again today would you provide substantially the same answers?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Konaj. My name is Veljko Djurdjic, and I'm a member of the team of defence for the accused Vlastimir Djordjevic, and with me here is my assistant, Ms. Marie O'Leary, a member of the Defence team. I will have a few questions for you. I would like to begin by asking you about your testimony today, your answers to the questions of the Prosecutor, Ms. Gopalan. So far you have made several statements, some were written, and there were also testimonies here before the Court, I believe in the Milosevic and Milutinovic cases. One of these testimonies was in 2002 and the other in 2006; am I correct?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Toward the end of the questioning by Ms. Gopalan you said that you didn't know when it was exactly that you had returned to Pec; and as far as I could observe, you did not actually witness the events in Pec from the moment when you left up until the moment when you returned; correct?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: From the 28th, when we left, that is, in 1999, up until the liberation of Kosova, I wasn't in Kosova; that is true.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And you don't know how your house happened to be damaged or the house of your father and your uncle because you weren't there, you did not actually witness this?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: That's also correct, but as I already told Ms. Gopalan -- she asked me how, in what state, I found these houses and Peje in general upon my return, not during the war. And upon my return, I found the houses in the state I already described.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. Thank you, Mr. Konaj. Now I would like to refer you to paragraph 28 of your statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But just let me say for the benefit of the Trial Chamber that the statement by Mr. Konaj in the English version and Albanian, I read the statements and I followed from numbers 1 to the end. So when I say "paragraph 25," this will be in the English version on page 5, or rather, paragraph 28, I apologise. So of page 5, paragraph 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Now, Witness, today you said that the bus driver who drove you from Pec said on the way -- on your way out, This is Serbia. This is not your country. Go to Albania. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: Correct. That's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And your recollection is better today than when you gave your statement - and I believe the second statement was on the 12th of June, 2001?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: I hope you will never go through that experience, and that experience can never be forgotten. I was expelled in the middle of the night with my whole family, most of it comprising women. I was the only man with my uncle amongst those women.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We are talking now about the time, the moment, when you actually boarded the bus for Prizren. So I am referring to that driver. Do you recall that you gave a statement in 2001 to the Prosecutor, or rather, to the investigator?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: I know you're referring to 2001 statement. I gave this statement to Garry Selsky, an investigator from The Hague who came to Albania. Then I gave another statement in Peje. So there were several statements, so I don't know which one in particular you're referring to. Can you please remind me.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: So regarding your statement from 2001 - and this is the reason why I would like you to listen very carefully so we can clear this up - Ms. Gopalan referred you to paragraph 28, or rather, paragraph 4 on page 5. The first paragraph is not a paragraph, really. It's just from -- a continuation from the previous page, but the fourth full paragraph. So did you say there that that comment referred to the driver who drove you from Prizren to the border, or the driver who drove you from Djakovica to Prizren? So let's just try and clarify this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Gopalan.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now it's more clear. The driver who brought us to Prizren was the same driver as in Peje, and he said the same thing, Go to Albania. This is not your country. These were his words. Whereas the driver who took us from Prizren to Vermice, he asked us kindly to stick to the main road and not to the sides because of the terrain that had been mined.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Gopalan.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. As the witness is being asked a number of questions about his statement, I wonder whether the statement should be called up on the screen so that it's easier for him to refer to the paragraphs that he's being asked questions about, or I have a hard copy of the Albanian which I could hand to him as well to ease the process.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: At the moment I've not discerned that the witness is in any way unable to recall the statement, but if at any time, sir, you need to check the statement, just indicate that, and we can let you have a copy or put one on the screen. Yes, Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I believe that the witness was able to clarify this on his own without the text, but I tend to agree with Ms. Gopalan that perhaps we should also have the statement on the screens. But I will ask Ms. Gopalan to do that once we come to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Now, let's go on, Mr. Konaj. Now, to paragraph 25 of your statement - in the English version that's page 5, the first full paragraph - this has to do with a man called Miki Stojanovic. For now, let me just say that you mentioned today during your testimony that this was a police officer who had a camouflage uniform on; is that correct? Did you say that today, earlier today? Have I understood you correctly?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: No, you have misunderstood me. I don't remember ever saying that he was dressed in uniform. He was in civilian clothes, whereas the others were dressed in both police uniforms and military uniforms. I never said that Miki Stojanovic was wearing uniform when I saw him.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: I wrote down, and I'm pretty certain, but never mind, you've corrected yourself now. But I believe that the first time that you did say that this man, Miki Stojanovic, wore a camouflage uniform on. But never mind, let's move on.

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: You probably misunderstood me.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. At the start of your testimony today you described the difference between those Pinzgauers. Now I would like to ask you, Could you please describe what one of those Pinzgauers looked like and what the other one looked like?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: Just one small clarification to avoid any misunderstanding. I want my words to be interpreted properly. I state with full responsibility that I never said today that Miki Stojanovic was dressed in uniform. He was amongst others who were dressed in police and military uniforms, so I want this to be corrected.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Konaj. I believe we've already cleared this up. Even if this was an error, an interpretation error or if you've misspoke, we've corrected it. But now this -- let's go back to these Pinzgauers, and I've asked you to describe the two Pinzgauers, one and then the other.

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: One was blue. I never served in the army, so I wasn't very clear in this, but I know that one of them was a police colour, blue, whereas the other was green, military colour. They were with big tires. They didn't have tracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Konaj, where are you employed currently?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: I do not work at the moment. I am in the construction business, but I'm not employed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. When you returned from Albania, did you have employment; and if so, what type?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: From 1999, when we were expelled, until this day, I was not employed with any body or organ.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: All right, but did you do any work since you returned from Albania up to this day? Perhaps as a private entrepreneur or any other type of job?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: I already said that privately I did do some construction business.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Can we understand this to mean that you have a company of your own?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Did you work for someone, for some company or some construction entrepreneur?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: I have acquaintances, family, friends, when they had need, for example, in Albania, I helped in the construction of a summer house of a friend of mine; but I was not employed with a company to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Konaj, have I understood you to say that you were born in Gornji Novo Selo in Djakovica municipality?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe the witness did not receive translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Was your father from this place?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did his father and his brothers, did they live in that village when you were born?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: Yes, they lived in a communal household.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. How many brothers did your father have?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: Two.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. When did your father leave or move from that village; and if he -- and if so, where did he go?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: An interesting question I would say. In 1956, when I was only 2, my grandfather, with my father and two uncles and other members of the family, sold their property and moved to Peje, to Karagaq neighbourhood.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. What was your father's occupation?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: During the time we lived in Novoselle, Gjakova municipality, he worked in the primary school at Novoselle e Ulet school, then at the primary school of Carrabreg in Decane. When we moved to Peje, he was a worker, a manual worker, in a factory in Peje.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you please tell me when and where did you complete your high school, or rather, intermediate education, the technical school that you attended.

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: In Prizren. I was there in 1969 as far as I remember, and completed secondary school in Peje. I don't remember for the moment the name of the school. I graduated in Peje.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. When reading your statements I found out that you did not serve in the army. Could you tell us why not?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: I wasn't summoned, and I did not go there to volunteer.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: You mean in the SFRY you were not -- you did not receive call-up papers, and you were not recruited?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: In these 55 years of my life, I was never recruited. Maybe they did send a summon, an invitation, to go and complete my military service, but I didn't receive it. I didn't receive the call-up.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Tell us, when did you get married?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: If I'm not mistaken, in 1970 or 1971 [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And your wife's family never inquired whether you had served in the army?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: Unfortunately, they were not the ones who were asked about our marriage. We loved each other, and we didn't ask much when we got married.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. But in our parts - and I mean that includes Pec and Djakovica - they say, He who is not fit for the army is not fit for marriage either, and that was always taken into account.

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: Your Honours, can I reply to this question or assertion with your permission?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's go out together, take me somewhere, and we can agree on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: All right. When we finish this. Tell me, when did you find employment?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: I started work in 1976 as a building inspector in Gjakove.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: You mean the municipality of Djakovica?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]...

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And then they didn't ask you whether you served in the army either?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... I didn't then. No, not even then.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: After that job, when did you find another one?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: I worked in Peje commune with contracts. The former secretariat for communal works, Aco was his name, I don't recall his last name, he employed us but with a contract. We worked there -- I worked there again as a building inspector, construction inspector.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: As of what year?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: I am sorry, but I am not certain about the year. It was before 1998, that's for sure. It was before 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In the times of the SFRY, were you a member of the League of Communists?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: No, I was never a member. I didn't have a card.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And after 1990 or 1991, at the introduction of the multi-party system, did you become a member of any of the political parties?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: Which party are you talking about?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Any. After 1991 the multi-party system was introduced.

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: Yes, I understand now. I was a member of the Democratic League of Kosova party, and after three or four years I am a member of the Presidency of the Christian Democratic Party of Kosova and member of the Presidency of the Peje branchs for this party.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you tell me, who was the president of the Christian Democratic Party of Kosovo when you were a member of the Presidency from Pec?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: The distinguished academician, Mark Krasniqi.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You've just said, and I also saw from the statements, that you were married and you had four children, including two sons. Tell me about your son Ndue, what was his occupation?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: At what time are you asking me about?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Well, let me first ask you a precise question: What kind of schooling did he have?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: He finished high school.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did he find -- did he have a job before he left for Switzerland?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And when did Ndue leave for Switzerland?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: I sent Ndue to Switzerland, as far as I remember, in 1999 together with Ilir, my uncle's son. They went through various routes until they reached there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And do you remember what season it was, what time of the year in 1999 when you sent him there?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: It was either spring or summer. I'm not sure. I don't know for sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. How about your son Bashkim, what schools did he complete?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: He finished the eight-year school.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Did he work after the primary school?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: Before he was 14, he went to my brother in Norway and he lives with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. What year was that?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: It was in December 1990.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And what is the name of your brother, he's your brother, not cousin; right?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: I have five brothers. Whom do you ask me about?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: The one in Norway.

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: His name is Gasper.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Did your son Bashkim return to Pec in 1999?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: No, he didn't, because he didn't have proper papers to be able to travel. He hadn't gotten his nationality yet at that time, a citizenship.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I call up the Defence Exhibit D002-6056.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Konaj, this is an aerial view -- this is an aerial view of Pec together with Lodja. Can you recognise it?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: No, I can't see anything I know. Loxhe, yes, now I see it. This is where I live in the vicinity of Loxhe marked with A.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: May I ask you to mark the place with a marker that you will be given.

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: It's here.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... place where your house used to be.

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: If this is the main road Peje-Decan, here -- this line here. This is the main road, Peje-Decan road. But as the crow flies it's 1 and a half kilometres. If you walk, it's 5 to 6 kilometres. I was wrong here.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You are a building technician, so please do it precisely on this nice map. Will you please put a number 1 to mark the location of your house.

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: Now I'm getting older and my hand isn't as firm as it used to be. If someone can help me, is this the Peje-Decan road? If someone shows me that this is the road, then I can tell you approximately where the house is.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Konaj, you put this dot, or several dots, on the map and said it was your house, this one that is --

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]...

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: -- fuller --

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: I said to you that I made a mistake because --

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: If this is a mistake, then let's wait a minute.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we erase this? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Let's try again, Mr. Konaj. First of all, your house, put a dot there and number 1.

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: I can't find my bearings because I need to know where the main road Peje-Decan is. I don't want to repeat the same mistake, so please let me or someone may help me indicate where the road is.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Konaj, do you see Pec here at the top of the picture and the road that goes out of it? All right. We'll come back to it later. Let's first go to Lodja.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I ask for D002-6057.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Konaj, you can probably understand the ground perspective much better.

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: I see here the village of Loxhe, something else.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us -- we see Lodja village and several settlements around it. Are there different hamlets within Lodja village; and if there are, please tell us where they are.

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: I don't know their hamlets. I don't know that. It has greatly changed now because there are many new constructions.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And do you know where Brezanik is?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: Berzhanik should be --

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... here?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: -- on this side here, a little bit higher. The shoe factory further on, yes, it must be higher than here.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: All right. So we can't see Brezanik here. Tell me then, did you know where the Vujosevic house was in Lodja?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Did you know that family from Brezanik?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: The last name is familiar, but this particular person you are asking me, I don't know. What was he doing? What kind of work did he do?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I didn't tell you the name of the person. I only asking you about the Vujosevic family. The name is Srdjan Vujosevic, if you know him.

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. So this is the broader view of Lodja.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we go back now to document D002-6056.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: That is the same thing seen from a greater distance and you should see your house?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... house here, neither in the first map.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Konaj, you see how much broader this is. You can see everything from Lodja to Pec, and you see the main road that we had seen previously.

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: This is what I can't find, the main road.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you this: Look to the left of this map. In the left corner, what is this feature? It's huge.

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: It is Italian village.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know -- do you see this road going uphill towards Pec from the Italian village?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Right. Parallel to it do you see this one going by Lodja, is it going to Decani?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: No, this is -- the one near Loxhe doesn't go in the direction of Decan. It goes in the middle -- between the Italian village and Loxhe there is the main road that goes in the direction of Peje, but I can't see the road here, unless this -- there is this one here.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Do you see on the right something going from the Italian village, a road going south from Pec by the Italian village south?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: I apologise, but I can't find my bearings here in this map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think, Mr. Djurdjic, we may have exhausted the possibilities here. The witness many times has said he cannot locate himself on this map.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. Let's move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Konaj, in which settlement is your house and your brother's house, the houses that you left in 1998 to move into your father's house in Pec?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: We called it Bellopoje. Bellopoje is a village where the Serbs and the Montenegrins used to live. Now the main road used to be called JNA, that is, the Yugoslav Army. They changed the names twice. Now it's called KLA 149, but at that time we used to call it Bel lopoje. Now they call it Dardanija 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Since we are talking about 1998 and 1999, let us use these terms, and if different terms were used in the statements, we'll deal with that. So this is Dardanija. Tell me, where was the house of Ana Konaj and who is Ana Konaj?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: Ana Konaj is my mother, the late one. Her house was also my house.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Did I understand this correctly, that's the house in Dardanija?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: I don't want to misunderstand you or you me. I said first it was called Bellopoje, Dardania, and many times they have changed the names. Now it's called KLA UCK 149, and it's a main road.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So regardless of the name change, that's the same house in that location, all the three names are the same thing?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: This is where the houses were looted.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Is your brother's house nearby as well?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: Yes, we lived in the same compound, let's say, in the same courtyard.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And what's the name of that brother?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: Pren Konaj is his name.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In 1999, was he in Pec when the war started?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: From 1993 my brothers were not living there. Only myself and my family was living there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And where was Pren?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: He was in Switzerland.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Was he a member of any political organisation; and if so, which one?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: They didn't have regular papers to come here. He was not registered or -- in any particular one, but he has contributed. Now he is LDK member.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: From Bijelo Polje to Lodja, how far is it by road?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: If you go by the main road, it may take 5 or 6 kilometres, whereas as the crow flies, it's not more than 1.5 kilometres. From where I live, I can see the entire Loxhe.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Was your house on higher ground?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: Yes, it is on a higher ground, and the house is tall. I used -- I build them before the war, and from there you can see Loxhe. I had a smaller house on the back.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And how far is it from this house where you lived to your father's house and your uncle's house?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: Are you talking about the house in the town where my parents live?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: Not more than 3 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: One last question before the break. Can you mark that house in Pec on this image, if it is visible, the place where the family house was and the uncle's house.

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: I can't see the centre here. I can't locate even the military barracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I think it's time for the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Very well. We must have the first break now. We resume at 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Konaj, do you remember that on the 12th of June, 2001, you made -- you gave a statement to an investigator of the Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: In general I know that I did give statements, but I know [as interpreted] which one in particular you're referring to. As I said, I gave two or three statements?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. This was a statement provided to Mr. Clifford Smith on the 12th of June, 2001. And in this statement on page 8 it says this statement of five pages was read back to me in the Albanian language and consists everything that I've said to the best of my knowledge and recollection; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: If you're referring to the statement in front of me, it is true that it is my statement -- or maybe I have a different one before me. It is true that I did give a statement, but I don't recall everything because it is in English, the statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Yes, we also have a translation into Albanian, and you've signed the statement in the English version but there is also a translation into Albanian following this English version.

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: I have the Albanian version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: So the transcript is clear, Mr. Djurdjic, you're referring to Exhibit P670? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. That's correct.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I remember it. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, let's take care of the administrative matters at the outset. So your first -- you first made or gave a statement, or rather, previously you also gave a statement on the 19th of April, 1999, to Mr. Garry Selsky. Do you remember?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: Yes, I remember Garry Selsky, I gave a statement to him in Albania.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We will return to these two statements, but let's now start with the statement you provided in 2001, and specifically paragraph 3. Can you tell me, please, whether you were in Bijelo Polje in early June in 1998 in your own house?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell me when you and your wife left the house in Bijelo Polje and went to the house in Pec?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: I had removed my mother and my daughters earlier and sent them to my father's house in Karagaq, and one night before Lodja was attacked, it was a Saturday, maybe the 5th, I'm not quite sure. Upon my wife insisting on moving from there, we left the house and went to Karagaq neighbourhood.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, if this happened on the 5th when you left, can you tell us when you took your mother and daughters from the house in Bijelo Polje?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: Several days prior to this date. We were the only ones still living there in that neighbourhood.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now please have on the screens D002-6040, page 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Konaj, do you recognise this area that we see in front of us?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: Beneath the photograph I read what it says, the text, and therefore I can tell it's part of Loxhe. However, I do not recognise the location depicted on the photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now please see photograph number 3. I apologise. If this was photo number 2, then I would like to see number 3. All right, you can leave this image on the screens.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Can you recognise this landscape now?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: No, I don't recognise the landscape; but I read the caption, and it says the village of Loxhe.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. I asked you -- I know that you can understand and read Serbian, but I just wanted to see if you could recognise this location that's depicted in the -- in the photograph. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could I now have D002-6064. I may have misspoken. D002-6040. No, that's the exhibit that I've already -- the one we've just seen. I apologise. So 6044. Page 5, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Konaj, do you recognise this building?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Page 6 on the screens.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Can you recognise anything now?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now please have page 7.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Can you recognise this?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And now page 8, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Do you recognise anything here, Mr. Konaj?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: I see that the same building is depicted on the photograph, but I don't recognise it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Konaj, have you heard that on the 6th of June, 1998, at 5.00 in the morning in Brezanik village, the house of the Vujosevic family was attacked and that this attack lasted two hours until a police patrol arrived? And that on this occasion the KLA took prisoner -- took as prisoner a policeman Perovic and another one and that two police officers were killed. Have you heard of that?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: No, I did not hear of that. I know that it was a Sunday when Loxhe was attacked, and we could hear gun-fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Just to tell you that those first photographs we saw were the -- depicted the trenches that we -- that were found there. And the other one was -- the other photographs were those of the house that was attacked by mortars, hand-held launchers. And now I would like to read something to you: "The fighting in Lodja built strong morale and a myth that there is a super-strong army which was -- which was comprised of soldiers of the 134th Brigade, fighters from Lodja near Morina, and volunteers who arrived from other villages. The enemy abandoned their tanks in the battle-field and began to withdraw from the barracks and the city of Pec, considering that Pec, too, had fallen. Aware that we did not have sufficient forces and arms to defend the city, we decided to fortify mined and strengthen Lodja so that it would become an insurpassable feature for the enemy and they couldn't get through." Have you ever heard this -- of this before, what I've just read out?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: It was impossible for me to hear or read something about that. What I know is that that was a severe attack on the village of Loxhe. It was even bombed from air in addition to ground attacks. I wasn't there on the spot, but we could hear the gun-fire because Loxhe is nearby where we live.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. On the 11th of July, 1998, the Serbian army, police, and paramilitary forces attacked Strellc. They immediately mobilised some personnel --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter could not catch the names.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- who was in charge of that territory, and I followed the entire operation by way of a 16-channel Motorola which I personally captured during the fighting in Lodja. The enemy abandoned two --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Djurdjic, what is it you are reading from?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is -- I was going to say where I was reading from. This is from a book by Mr. Arber Ahmetaj and Sefedjin Krasniqi: "Thus Spoke Tahir Zemaj, Part II."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I do not see the purpose of what you are doing at the moment. If the witness is familiar with the book, he may be able to verify its contents; if he isn't familiar with the book, he may be able to say, I know something about that. But at the moment so far in his evidence he shows no sign of any familiarity at all with the subject matter. So why are you continuing to quote passages from this book to the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. This was the last paragraph that I was going to quote, the reason being that in the last sentence of this paragraph there is something, a reference to the witness statement, this witness's statement, regarding the situation in the field in Lodja. The portion that says: "After the fighting when a relative peace set in, some heros appeared who were boasting about how many Serbs they had killed or how many houses they had searched and looted."

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And to clarify, sir, I've already mentioned this book - and this was on pages 92 and 95 of this book - and it refers to your --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Djurdjic, if you are saying that there is something in that book which is based upon the statement of this witness, you should put that particular issue to him and see whether he agrees he made the words or is aware that his statement was used in the book. Otherwise, the book is of no use at all in these proceedings. And it's the bit that relates to him which should be the subject of your questioning.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Konaj, have you heard of or read this second part of the book, "The Conversation With Mr. Zemaj," that I've just read out here?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: I did not read this book. I know that the book was published. It was put to me in my previous testimony that I published the book. I didn't do that. I only know that it was published, but I never read the book itself. Your Honour, I have a request.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as I know, I've been called to testify here about the statement that I gave in Albania regarding the situation of the population in Peje at the time. The questions of Mr. Djurdjic I would like to be focused on the statements that I gave earlier. Secondly, he put to me that what they say in our parts, Those who are not fit for army are not fit for marriage, and that really hurt me. The question I put now is: How come I have four children with my own wife? I was married in 1973 not in 1971, as it is recorded here. This is the clarification I wanted to make. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I'm sure, Mr. Konaj, that the reference to your marriage is one that was not intended as you have understood it. In any event, frankly it seems to have nothing to do with the issues in this case. Insofar as you may be questioned about some matters that are outside the scope of your statement, it is for this Chamber to determine whether Mr. Djurdjic is going into irrelevant areas; and where that occurs, we will stop the questions. Now, Mr. Djurdjic, we were at the point where the witness has indicated with respect to the book that although he knew of it, he hadn't published it and he's never read it. Now, I think that puts an end to the questioning about the book. Now, do you have some other matter now you wish to ask about?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I have finished with that topic anyway, and I was about to move to a new one.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Konaj, I am really sorry. I had no intention of offending you. When I quoted our popular saying, I was only inquiring how it was possible that you were never called up into the army. I never meant to hurt you. And if you feel hurt, I sincerely apologise. And you must know it was never intended that way. But this last thing I put to you has to do a part of your statement, paragraph 3 in fact. That's the passage from your 1998 statement, and I had come to a point --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Did you mean 1998?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1999, in fact, when he gave his first statement in Tirana, relating to events from 1998, that is, after what happened in Lodja.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And that is, Mr. Konaj, the part where you left to your father's, that is, uncle's house, and heard that the police had been to look for you. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. I was with a friend of mine who was the principal of the school in Peje, Shaqir Studenica is his name. And we parted. He went to his home, I went to my home; but on the way I stopped at a coffee shop and then Shaqir came and told me that my daughter had called him, asking him to tell me to go home immediately because something had happened. We set off for home on two bikes to my father's home. In the vicinity of the mosque I asked him, What has happened? Tell me, please. Have they killed someone? He said, They have killed someone but have left the corpse in your house, in Bellopoje. The police came to my house. That is true.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... and you went to the police in Pec with your uncle, if I'm not mistaken?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: That's correct. They had left instructions that if I didn't report, they would come back at any time to make sure that I went back. It was 4.00 in the afternoon when I went back. About 5.00 we went to the police. It was on the second floor of the building that we went to if I remember right.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Konaj, were you advised on that occasion -- occasion that in the courtyard of Ana Konaj in Brezanik on the 6th of July, 1998, a body was found, a female body?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: That's why the police came to my father's house and looked for the owner where I used to live in the new house in Bellopoje. That's why they went to search for us there, and that's why I went to the police. Initially they took my uncle and asked him to identify the corpse; but when we went, it was in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So the police were interested only because a woman who happened to be in your house in Brezanik was killed?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: When they entered my uncle's house, he was there with his two daughters watching television. They addressed him with these words, as he told me. They didn't know my name and they said to him, In the house of your brother's son, someone -- a policeman was killed. Then they said, Someone was killed. Then you have to come and identify the corpse. When he went there he saw that there was an old woman whom later I realised it was Marlise [as interpreted] Hoti's mother, and they were my neighbours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And finally was it established that it was a person from Ivangrad?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: I am sorry, but it was established that she was my neighbour, two houses away from mine, Marlise's mother. I don't know if she is from Ivangrad to this day but I know that she is a Bosnian and that to this day her sons live there as my neighbours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Was her name Hoti, Nazmije? That is Nazmije Hoti?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: Yes. We used to call her "Tota Naze."

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Would I be right in saying that you did not see personally how your house was damaged in 1998 and Bijelo Polje, that is, in Brezanik?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: It is as you say. It was after three or four days, I'm not sure, that with my friend Shaqir they had recognised an inspector who used to work in the SUP from Raushiq I think. I didn't mention this detail before. They took us with two cars. He came with his own car, my friend with his own car. We went to the house and we took pictures. My friend Shaqir Studenica said to the inspector, You simply had to use a match to set fire to what had remained. Very little had remained of the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I think the photographs are part of your statement, so we can see exactly what remained of the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I now call up Defence Exhibit D002-6058. Can we zoom in.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Konaj, this is an image of Pec. Could you show us your father's and your uncle's house?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: There are many houses here, and it's difficult for me to identify them. It was what we call Domi i Armales, above, Domi i Armales. Dom Armije we call, army's house. From there it's not more than 50 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Pec is a large town, Mr. Konaj. I'm not asking you to show me the house, but the area in which your house was.

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: The centre of the town, in the centre, across the centre, used to be this army's house. Above it is Kulla e Sheremetit, and then comes my house, my father's house. I'm telling you, it's difficult for me to identify the centre here.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: You can't identify even the centre of the hotel where the Metohija Hotel was and the court?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: Frankly speaking, I cannot. I can't see it here. I cannot locate it precisely.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: You don't recognise a single feature here?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: It seems to me that here is Soliter. I think Soliter must be here. If I'm not mistaken, Soliter is here.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Will you put a number 1 there and explain what you just said about this skyscraper, Soliter you call it.

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: It's a 12-storey building across the SUP building or former SUP -- at least this is what seems to me to be. It's a building, 12-storey building, we used to call -- even now we call it Soliter.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Relative to that building, where was your father's and uncle's house?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: Relative to that building, then on the left-hand side, if I'm not mistaken, this part looks like the centre. Then the house must be here, somewhere here, my father's house, that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Could you put an X in the area of Pec where your father's house could be?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: I'm not very sure, but it must be here.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you put a number 2 there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And we'll note that it's the witness's father's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Relative to your father's house, could you mark Kameni Most, the stone bridge -- or let us take it slowly. What is closer, because there are several features, is the bus station somewhere near?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: I'm telling you that I'm not very sure about what I am marking here. If the Soliter is here, then on the right side is a bus station; then on the left side where I put 2, if this is the centre, is my father's house. Ura e Gurit must be 150 metres from my father's house. Stone bridge on the right side.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Konaj. Of course you can't mark the exact place, but in order to be able to understand your statement and your movements better, just mark it -- show us these buildings approximately. Could you mark the bus station, for instance, first?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: I'm repeating what I put 1 on the right side, approximately here must be the bus station, if Soliter is where I think it is, but I'm not sure. I'm surprised at myself for not being able to locate these features.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Could you find the Catholic church?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: On the right-hand side, near patriarchate, which is not more than 250, 300 metres away.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Could you then please write -- that is, mark the patriarchy.

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: I apologise with -- because I am simply making suppositions here. I'm not 100 per cent sure. I'm repeating it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I fear, Mr. Djurdjic, we're not getting anywhere. We've had two successful markings, but the witness keeps repeating he's not sure if they are correct. And he is not able to identify any other location you have mentioned, none of which, as far as I can tell, are mentioned in the statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, all the locations mentioned were referred to in the statement. I have five or six more locations I wanted to ask him about but -- all right. Never mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: I've been to Pec ten times, Mr. Konaj, and I can see the patriarchy, that is, the Orthodox bishopric, but all right, never mind. You don't need to look at the map anymore. Did you own a passenger vehicle in March 1999?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: Not one but two.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Where were they?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: I had an Audi 80, black colour. I kept that at my father's house, and they destroyed it there, and they brought it to me on the 28th in the centre of Peje, and I gave them some money for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And how about the second vehicle?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: It was also the same mark, Audi 80. It was white colour. I went to Ulqin with it in 1998 together with my neighbour with both my Audis. I left the white Audi there, and I used the black one to return home.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Tell me, what are paramilitary forces? How do you understand that term?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: The usual Yugoslav Army, the regular army, had one solid-colour uniform, green one. By paramilitaries we refer to the people dressed in camouflage uniforms or camouflage trousers and T-shirt above and so on. Members who comprised Peje inhabitants, those that joined such forces, this is what we called paramilitaries.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know what military reserve is?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: I have explained even earlier that I was not -- I didn't do my military service, but I knew that there were military reservists. This is all I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Do you think there is a difference between reserve military forces and active military forces?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: What can I say? I know that the active military forces should abide by discipline in their service, whereas those that you call reservists mobilise in case of need.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Do you know at the beginning of the war or at the run-up to the war, was there a mobilisation call-up?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Can you exclude the possibility that these persons whom you call paramilitary units were in fact a military reserve unit?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: I do not exclude that possibility, but I have seen also my neighbours, Peje inhabitants, who were dressed in those camouflage uniforms. And I saw them armed, wandering around the streets of Peje and in the Catholic cemeteries and in the Muslim one.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Konaj. In paragraph 10 of your 2001 statement, you state the following: "When we arrived at the petrol station, there were two Pinzgauers there, one military and one police Pinzgauer." That part of the statement is missing from when you first gave a statement in 1999.

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: I don't know whether that is missing or not. I don't know whether that question was asked of me or whether the interpreter has interpreted my answer. I don't know that.
