But the fact is that once we passed the stone bridge there are some steps and there was a gas station which is still today some 25 metres away from there. And it is true that there were two Pinzgauers there, one police, one military.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, I believe those petrol stations are still there. I'm just saying that this reference is missing from the 1999 statement, but let's move on. In paragraph 18 from your 2001 statement, I'd like you to explain one thing. You said: "I asked Salih Dreshaj to give a ride to my mother and my mother-in-law." Did he do that?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: I didn't say at Salih Dreshaj's place. On the 27th to the 28th we went to Salih Dreshaj's house, who is my best man. The following day, I told Salih Dreshaj's son, Riza, to take my mother and my mother-in-law with him in the car. He didn't want to, but I kind of forced him to take the two old women with him because they were not feeling well. So Riza left with his wife and his children and my mother and my mother-in-law in his car, whereas we, the others, walked. This is when we left that place. I didn't say that my -- that Salih took me to the place where my mother was. My mother was with me all the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You've explained that all, and that's what is stated also in your statement, and now I have had the clarification as well. Now, in paragraph 19 you said: "We left the house and joined the crowd leaving Salih behind." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Djurdjic, the witness hasn't got the statement in front of him, and the reason for that is that we still have on the screen the Google aerial photograph of Pec. Do you want those two markings preserved as an exhibit or not?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, since the witness wasn't sure of what he was marking, I do not suggest that we enter this into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. It can be removed then, and we'll bring up the statement so that the witness can follow your questions more clearly.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. This is Exhibit P670. Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter correction.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Witness, what I would like to ask you about now is on page 6, of the Albanian version, paragraph 20, or rather, page 6, the second paragraph from the bottom. And in the English version this is on page 4, one, two, three, four, the fifth paragraph from the top. So: "We left the house, joined the crowds, leaving Salih there." Is that correct, Mr. Konaj?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: Yes. He left his father there because I forced his son to take my mother and mother-in-law in his car.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I would like to direct you to paragraph 23. In the Albanian version that's on page 7, from the top, the third paragraph, "around 1900 hours," and in the English version this would be on page 4. From the bottom, the second paragraph. Mr. Konaj, you say here: "About 7.00 p.m. three military tanks entered the centre of town. One was being towed by another. Two of these tanks pointed their barrels towards the people. It caused great fear. The tanks left both 2000 hours and the lights in the city went out. The sky was clear. There was a moon." Now, this entire paragraph is missing from your statement of 1999.

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: It is true that these two tanks came. One was being towed by another, probably was not working properly. People were displaced, that is also true. It is also true that one of them manning the tank was rotating the barrel of the tank. It is true that it caused great fear. I personally was in fear let alone the children and the women.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Konaj, my question was related to what you have read to us, that this was not mentioned in April 1999, in your statement, which was some 20 days after the event.

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: I don't know how that could happen, but I know very well that I gave a statement for nine hours or so in Albania. I am quite sure that I mentioned this on that occasion, and that's why the representative of this honoured Court insisted on the details of the places, where I stayed, what happened and so on. So I'm quite surprised how this passage did not enter that statement of 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I'd like to refer you to paragraph 25 of your 2001 statement, that's the portion relating to Miki Stojanovic. Again Miki is mentioned. When in 1999 you gave your statement, you said the following about Mr. Stojanovic: "I recognised a Serb in civilian clothes. His name was Miki Stojanovic and nicknamed Lapoc. He was a cafe owner in the neighbourhood called Piskote just outside Gjakove. He was a man who gave -- he didn't -- he wasn't doing anything, he just stood there." Whereas in paragraph 25 of this statement, the 2001 statement, you say: "I recognised one of the Serbs in civilian clothes. His name was Miki Stojanovic, nicknamed Lapoc. He was the owner of a cafe in the neighbourhood called Piskote just outside Djakovica. He was the man who gave the order to separate the men from the others. I have been told that in my first statement I said that Lapoc did not say anything. This must be an interpretation error because he was definitely the man who gave the order, although it was not carried out." So where does this discrepancy come from related to this person in your two statements?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: Again, I have no idea why this mistake occurred. It is true that I knew Miki Stojanovic from before. I used to work with his brother in Gjakove municipality. It is true that he was there; he was dressed in civilian clothes. Sometimes the interpretation is done very fast and sentences can be slightly changed. It is true that he was dressed in civilian clothes. He approached the driver of the bus where I was with my family and other people, and he said to the driver, All the men should get off the bus and come out. So the driver - I'm calling him a soldier because he was dressed in uniform - said to him, I have my orders, and I'm not allowing you to get anyone off this bus. There was a truck covered with tarpaulin in front of the bus. They were dressed in camouflaged uniforms. Whoever they caught, they beat them with their rifle-butts, and the blood could be seen even on the --

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... meet again --

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... bus where we were. And the police said to the driver, We will see once you're back here.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In paragraph 27 of your 2001 statement you state: "When we arrived there about 1.00 to 1.30 a.m., we stopped at the junction that leads to Vermice. The driver told us to get off and said, Go to Albania. This is not your place. This is great Serbia. They turned the buses and trucks around and drove away." In your 1999 statement, there is no mention of this.

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: Again, this surprises me. It is true what he said to us, There's no place for you here, this is Serbia, go to your own country, go to Albania.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. One more thing, in paragraph 29 of your 12th June 2001 statement you say: "The men were searched and the women's purses were checked." This is a reference to the time when you were on the border. This too is missing from your 1999 statement.

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: Again, it surprises me how come I did not mention that. It is true that we were told at the border to throw all our personal documentation in that box. It is true that they searched the bags of the women. I pretended to have thrown my ID in the box; but, in fact, I didn't throw it, and I still have it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the witness statement of 19th April 1999, which is a Defence document, D002-6026, I move to have it adopted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be assigned D00093, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Konaj, I apologise once again. It was not my intention to offend you. These were all the questions I had for you today.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. My cross-examination is over.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Djurdjic. Ms. Gopalan, re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Mr. Konaj, I have a few questions for you. Defence counsel asked you a number of questions today about your statement from 2001.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: I'd like to call up the statement. The exhibit is P670, both the English and the Albanian, please. Could we please go to page 2 of the English and page 2 of the Albanian. For the Albanian could we go to the next page, please, it should be page 3.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Mr. Konaj, could you please read out the first sentence of the statement in Albanian, so the line that appears below the heading "witness statement."

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: "Interviewer's note: This statement is based on an informal statement taken on 19th April 1999, my name is Ndrec Konaj" --

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Konaj, that's sufficient.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: I'd now like to call up the statement of 1999 which was recently tendered into evidence. The exhibit number is D93. And in both the English and the Albanian could we please go to the last pages. For the English could we go to the previous page, please, not the last but page 5.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Mr. Konaj, in the Albanian version of your 1999 statement that you have on the screen before you, could you read the last paragraph on that page.

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: "The statement in English has not been read back to me. I was asked to speak about different periods of time, and I can recall other events if that is requested of me. I'm ready to testify."

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Konaj. Now, you were also asked some questions about the units that you saw in Pec.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: For the record, this is line 45, 9.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: And you mentioned that you saw your neighbours, Peje inhabitants, who were dressed in camouflage uniforms and that they were armed. Do you recall that section of your testimony today, Mr. Konaj?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: Yes, I do, because those who were in the neighbourhood where I lived, in Berzhanik or Dardanija or now called UCK Street, they were dressed in camouflage uniforms, they were stationed in the Muslim and Catholic cemeteries. This is true.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Konaj. Just to clarify, when was it you saw these individuals who were dressed in camouflage uniforms, approximately when?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: In 1998 when I left my house to go to my father's house. From my father's house then I went to Ulqin, and I saw them on the way to Ulqin in Montenegro at a location in Rrozhaja. I don't remember the name of the border crossing there.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you. And you said that they were your neighbours, Peje inhabitants. Do you know their names?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: If you're referring to the events at the stone bridge, I only knew them by sight. Of course when you are living in a city and go out on the streets every day, you can tell people by sight; but I didn't know their names. I never knew them.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Perhaps my question wasn't clear, Mr. Konaj. This morning you were asked by Defence counsel whether you knew the deference between persons who were paramilitary units or those who were military reserve units and your answer was: "A. I do not exclude that possibility, but I have seen also my neighbours, Peje inhabitants, who were dressed in those camouflage uniforms, and I saw them armed around the streets of Peje and in the Catholic cemeteries and the Muslim one." Now, these are the people that I am asking you questions about, the armed people who you saw in the Catholic cemetery and close to the Muslim cemetery. When was it that you saw them there?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: In 1998 and later on in 1999 after I returned from Ulqin and before we were expelled.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you. And you mentioned that they were armed. Do you know who armed them?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: No, but they did have automatic rifles. I don't know if they had any side weapon, but I could see the automatic rifles hanging on their shoulders. The same ones could be seen in the centre on the 28th when we left with the last bus.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you. And these neighbours of yours who you saw in the Catholic cemetery, do you recall any of their names?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: To tell you the truth, we always addressed each other with the word "neighbour," "neighbour." So when the police came to look for me at my uncle's house, they didn't even know my name. They knew only the names of my sons, the children played with each other. Slavko was one of my neighbours, then Mile Vasic was also a neighbour of mine. He was a neighbour from Bellopoje. He had a cafe at Stari Most, the stone bridge. And from this cafeteria two people with camouflage uniforms came out.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Konaj. Now, just going back to these neighbours who you mentioned, do you know what ethnicity they were?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: Serbs. Maybe they were even Montenegrins, but I never asked them if they were Serbs or Montenegrins. Serb ethnicity.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Konaj. I have no further questions for you.

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: [In English] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: Mr. Konaj, I want to take you back to your description of the attack on the village of Lodja, and you said there was a severe attack on the village of Lodja. It was even bombed from the air in addition to the ground attack. Who bombed it from the air?

utterances.speaker: NDREC KONAJ
utterances.text: The members of the Yugoslav Army -- I mean the aircraft. I'm not being specific here, whether it was a regular Yugoslav Army, but the aircraft was of Yugoslav Army.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Konaj, that concludes the questions for you. The Chamber would like to thank you for coming yet again to The Hague and for the assistance that you've been able to give us. We now have your evidence today together with your statements and the transcripts of the evidence you've given in previous trials. We thank you for that which will be of assistance to us in due course. The court officer will show you out, and you are, of course, free to return to your normal activities.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. May God help you in your work.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Clearly this is a convenient time for the second break which we must take now. We will resume at 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. D'Ascoli.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. We're ready with the next witness, and it's Mr. Edison Zatriqi. And his evidence relates to paragraphs 72(e) and 77 of the indictment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good afternoon. Would you please read aloud the affirmation on the card which is shown to you now.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Please sit down.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. D'Ascoli has some questions for you.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness. Would you please state your full name for the record, please.

utterances.speaker: EDISON ZATRIQI
utterances.text: My name is Edison Zatriqi.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: And could you please state your date of birth.

utterances.speaker: EDISON ZATRIQI
utterances.text: I was born on the 5th of December, 1956.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: And where were you born, Mr. Zatriqi?

utterances.speaker: EDISON ZATRIQI
utterances.text: I was born in Peje.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Where are you currently living?

utterances.speaker: EDISON ZATRIQI
utterances.text: In the same town, in Peje.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Thank you. And which is your current occupation, Mr. Zatriqi?

utterances.speaker: EDISON ZATRIQI
utterances.text: Currently I work with the OSCE, their regional office. I work in the transport department as a driver.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Thank you. Sir, did you provide a statement to representative of the Office of the Prosecutor in June 2001 and subsequently an addendum to that statement in January 2002?

utterances.speaker: EDISON ZATRIQI
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: And have you recently had the opportunity to review this statement?

utterances.speaker: EDISON ZATRIQI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Are you satisfied that the information contained in them is true and accurate to the best of your knowledge and belief?

utterances.speaker: EDISON ZATRIQI
utterances.text: Absolutely, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: And, sir, did you also testify before this Tribunal in the Milutinovic et al. case in September 2006?

utterances.speaker: EDISON ZATRIQI
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: And have you recently had the opportunity to review also this previous testimony in the Milutinovic et al. case?

utterances.speaker: EDISON ZATRIQI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: And if you were asked the same question today, would you provide substantially the same answers and would you testify in the same way?

utterances.speaker: EDISON ZATRIQI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'd like to tender into evidence both the witness statement and the transcript. The witness statement are the 65 ter number 02347.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be assigned P00672, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: And the witness's testimony in the Milutinovic et al. case is the 65 ter number 05051.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be assigned P00673, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Thank you. I will now read a summary of this witness's evidence. The witness describes the events in Peje on the 27th and the 28th of March, 1999, which led to the expulsion of Kosovo Albanians from the area. The witness was the director of a coach company called Flamingo Tours which owned three coaches. On the 23rd of March, 1999, the witness was ordered to go to the place where his buses were, and there two policemen took away these three buses. When he asked for documentation, one of the policemen pointed his gun at the witness and threatened him. On the 27th of March, 1999, the witness was in his house in the Sahat Kula neighbourhood of Peje, when he witnessed Serb military shelling the carry of Kapeshnica from the hospital yard and the secondary school. The witness moved to the house of a relative in the Jarina neighbourhood in Peje. The following day the witness and his family joined a long convoy of vehicles which was being directed towards Montenegro by armed police and armed civilians. While in the convoy, the witness saw one of his buses full of people. The witness returned to Peje in July 1999 and found that his house, business offices, and coaches had been burnt. This is the end of the in-court summary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Mr. Zatriqi, as you know, the Trial Chamber now already has before it your previous statement and testimony. Therefore, I'll just have some -- a few questions for you in relation to the events in Peje in March 1999. Sir, in your statement - and this is paragraph 10 at the end of page 2 in the English version - you say that the Serb military started shelling Peje on the early morning of the 27th of March, 1999. Mr. Zatriqi, I wanted to ask you whether this is something that you saw yourself with your own eyes?

utterances.speaker: EDISON ZATRIQI
utterances.text: Yes, it is true that I saw the shelling with my own eyes.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: And can you please tell us from where you observed all this?

utterances.speaker: EDISON ZATRIQI
utterances.text: My house is in such a position that allows me to see the direction from where these shells were fired and where they were directed at. These shells were flying over my -- the roof of my house. I was moving in the house from the third floor to the part behind the house. Therefore, I could clearly see the shelling from where they were firing shells and what they targeted. The shells fell in a neighbourhood which is opposite to our neighbourhood. It is called Kapeshnica.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Sir, I'm going to show you a map of the town of Peje.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Can I please have on the screen the 65 ter number 00615, which is the Kosovo atlas, and I would need page 46 of this atlas, please. If you can scroll down, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Sir, can you see the map, and do you recognise Peje and this neighbourhood?

utterances.speaker: EDISON ZATRIQI
utterances.text: Yes, I can clearly see the map.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Can we please go down a little bit more.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Sir, I understand from your statement in paragraph 10, page 2, that your house is located in the neighbourhood called Sahat Kula, and I was wondering whether you can see this neighbourhood on the map.

utterances.speaker: EDISON ZATRIQI
utterances.text: The neighbourhood on this map is marked with the name Puhovci.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Therefore, is Puhovci and Sahat Kula, are they the same neighbourhood?

utterances.speaker: EDISON ZATRIQI
utterances.text: Yes, you can say that. When you say Puhovci I know what you're referring to, and if you use Sahat Kula I will know that you referred to this neighbourhood.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Okay. Would you be able to locate your house in -- on the map in the neighbourhood of Sahat Kula? We can move the map also down or up if you need.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Maybe all the way down, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Is it better like this?

utterances.speaker: EDISON ZATRIQI
utterances.text: Yes, it's better. It is right by the Catholic church.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: You will be provided with a pen, and if you're able to -- to indicate where your house would be, could you please mark it with a dot and put a number 1 close to it.

utterances.speaker: EDISON ZATRIQI
utterances.text: It should be here approximately, by the road.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Can you mark more clearly the number 1, please, because I cannot see it.

utterances.speaker: EDISON ZATRIQI
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: So for the record the witness has put a blue dot and a number 1 close to it to indicate the place where his house was.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Thank you. In that same paragraph of your statement, and there was page 2, paragraph 10, you indicated that on the 27th of March the shelling was coming from the hospital and the school. Sir, would you be able to indicate on this map also where the hospital and the school were?

utterances.speaker: EDISON ZATRIQI
utterances.text: Here is the school, the secondary school or high school --

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: If you could -- could you please mark it with the letter S for school and H for hospital.

utterances.speaker: EDISON ZATRIQI
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Could you mark more precisely the letter H because the -- sorry.

utterances.speaker: EDISON ZATRIQI
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. And in which direction was the shelling going on that morning from -- I mean from the school and from the hospital? If you could maybe like draw two arrows from the school and the hospital to indicate the direction of the fire and of the shelling.

utterances.speaker: EDISON ZATRIQI
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Thank you. So who was firing from the school and from the hospital towards the neighbourhood of Kapeshnica?

utterances.speaker: EDISON ZATRIQI
utterances.text: The Serb army was shelling with its tanks.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Did you see that yourself?

utterances.speaker: EDISON ZATRIQI
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Okay. With regard to the neighbourhood of Kapeshnica, by whom was it inhabited?

utterances.speaker: EDISON ZATRIQI
utterances.text: The Kapeshnica neighbourhood was inhabited exclusively by Albanians.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Okay. If we go back to the map, sir, do you also see the neighbourhood of Jarina on this map?

utterances.speaker: EDISON ZATRIQI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: And would you be able to indicate where your aunt's house in Jarina was?

utterances.speaker: EDISON ZATRIQI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Could you indicate it with a dot and place a number 2 close to it, please?

utterances.speaker: EDISON ZATRIQI
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would like to tender this exhibit as marked by the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Mr. Zatriqi, as we --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be assigned P00674, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Mr. Zatriqi, as we were speaking about this shelling by the Serb army, can you tell us for how long did the shelling go on?

utterances.speaker: EDISON ZATRIQI
utterances.text: The shelling began early in the morning. As I stated earlier, one of the reasons I left the house was the shelling itself. Therefore, I'm not able to say for how long it continued because I went to another part of the town. However, based on the blasts, on the explosions, I can say that it lasted for at least two or three hours.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Can you then clarify the reasons why you left your house on that morning, on the morning of the 27th of March.

utterances.speaker: EDISON ZATRIQI
utterances.text: We left the house on the 27th of March because a night earlier, a night between the 26th and the 27th, there was firing at our house. My family and I and my parents were sheltered in the basement of the house. I was moving in the house itself throughout this time, going from one part to another part of the house. And when the shelling started in the morning, we decided to leave. I spoke with my aunt who lives in Jarina. I asked her about the situation in Jarina. She said that the night was quiet compared to the situation in our neighbourhood. Therefore, we all decided to leave the house and to go to Jarina, to this other part of the town.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Sir, can I ask you whether you had the chance of seeing who was firing at your house?

utterances.speaker: EDISON ZATRIQI
utterances.text: As I've already said, from moving from one part to another part of the house, I could see clearly that early in the morning at around 2.00 or 3.00 in the morning, Furgon, police Furgon vehicle stopped near the house, spoke to my neighbours. There were also neighbours of mine who were armed. And an hour later, they started to fire in the direction of the house.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: And did you see this yourself from your house?

utterances.speaker: EDISON ZATRIQI
utterances.text: Yes, I saw it with my own eyes.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: And who were these neighbours of yours that you mentioned?

utterances.speaker: EDISON ZATRIQI
utterances.text: It was not my neighbours who shot, but persons who came out of this minivan, as many as could be accommodated in a minivan, and they were dressed in police uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: And you said: "They were together with these policemen also neighbours of mine who were armed." I'm just reading your previous answer from the transcript.

utterances.speaker: EDISON ZATRIQI
utterances.text: These were my neighbours who, during the night, stood armed and moved about the neighbourhood, and as I said earlier in -- near my house there were some neighbours who were armed. And when the minivan came, I saw it with my own eyes, and they talked with these neighbours. And then they left, and the policemen started to shoot.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: I'm sorry, who talked with these neighbours?

utterances.speaker: EDISON ZATRIQI
utterances.text: One of the policemen who came out of the minivan.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: And what was the ethnicity of your neighbours?

utterances.speaker: EDISON ZATRIQI
utterances.text: These neighbours who moved about the neighbourhood armed were Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Okay, sir. I'll move to the part of your statement where you describe that you left your aunt's house and Peje on the 28th of March and you joined a convoy of other vehicles. Can you tell this Court why you and your family left your aunt's house in the town of Peje on the 28th of March.

utterances.speaker: EDISON ZATRIQI
utterances.text: On Saturday, on the 27th, when we left our house and went to Jarina at my aunt's house, it was relatively calm there. And the night was, as I said, relatively calm, with the exception of the fact that we saw a very powerful reflector lightening the place around there. In the morning when we woke up, at about 8.00, 8.30 I think it was, a police car came and stopped at the entrance to this street because this neighbourhood has two exits and two entrances. From the police van came out the policemen who in a loud voice ordered us that in five minutes we leave the houses, and we -- some families who were there who had cars got on the cars and left the house.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: And just to clarify, when you say: "... in the morning when we woke up, at about 8.00, 8.30 ..." which morning do you mean, which day, and where were you that morning?

utterances.speaker: EDISON ZATRIQI
utterances.text: In the morning of Sunday, that is, on the 28th of March.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Where were you on that day?

utterances.speaker: EDISON ZATRIQI
utterances.text: Until the morning of the 28th I was at my aunt's house. We went there on the 27th. We slept there, if you like, and in the morning we were obliged to leave.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: And, sir, at page 3, paragraph 2, of your statement you say that that morning, on the 28th, you joined this convoy directed towards Rozaje. Can you please describe that convoy and who were the people that you saw in that convoy?

utterances.speaker: EDISON ZATRIQI
utterances.text: My aunt's neighbourhood is in a parallel street with one of the main streets of Peje, and the second entry and exit points were free. They -- it linked with the main road. At that moment, I saw many cars in a convoy which I joined. I saw also many people who were walking. Maybe they didn't have vehicles, so they walked in the same direction that we walked.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: And can you specify who these people were?

utterances.speaker: EDISON ZATRIQI
utterances.text: These people I may assure you were all Albanians and all evicted from their homes, and they simply walked in the same direction that we drove with our cars.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Sir, in the same paragraph and still paragraph 2, page 3, you also mentioned that there were armed police and armed civilians at various road junctions and that these armed police and civilians were directing you towards Montenegro. Can you explain what you mean for that and -- for example, could you go in any other direction?

utterances.speaker: EDISON ZATRIQI
utterances.text: When we got to the main road, the only direction open for us was that towards junction. At the junction there were police. There was a policeman, armed policeman of course, who directed us towards Montenegro. The same was true at two other junctions. So there was no choice for us. I and the other people like me were obliged to go in that direction, irrespective of whether they were driving or walking. So everyone was heading towards Montenegro.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: And, sir, could you estimate approximately how many people were in the convoy?

utterances.speaker: EDISON ZATRIQI
utterances.text: I wouldn't be able to give you figures because I was there, but there were other people behind me, so I didn't know where the end of it was. I know only that it was a very long convoy.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: And by "a very long convoy," do you mean vehicles and people together or -- if you can specify, please.

utterances.speaker: EDISON ZATRIQI
utterances.text: Yes, the convoy consisted of people walking as well as cars -- driving cars or other vehicles driving.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Zatriqi.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I don't have further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. D'Ascoli. Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours, but I have a request to make. In view of the fact that we have heard many new facts from the witness that he hasn't said before, in order for me to cross-examine him more efficiently and more quickly, I would appreciate it if you would allow me to start with my cross-examination tomorrow and I will be very quick with this witness because I have to inquire about some things that he's mentioned here for the first time, and there are some ten or so new facts that he's put forth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The Chamber would prefer you, Mr. Djurdjic, to use the 15 minutes we have. There may be some new matters raised, but they can be looked at overnight. So that if you would proceed with your cross-examination now.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Zatriqi, my name is Veljko Djurdjic, and I'm a member of the Defence team of the accused, Vlastimir Djordjevic; and with me today is Ms. Marie O'Leary, who is a member of the Defence team. I have some questions for you, and if you don't understand something please let me know and I will try to rephrase my question so that you can then answer it. Tell me, Mr. Zatriqi, you were born in Pec in 1956. Do you have any brothers or sisters?

utterances.speaker: EDISON ZATRIQI
utterances.text: Yes, I have one brother and one sister.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In 1999, were your parents, your father and mother, alive?

utterances.speaker: EDISON ZATRIQI
utterances.text: Yes, they are still alive.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank God. Now tell me, did you live separately from your parents, away from your parents, in 1999?

utterances.speaker: EDISON ZATRIQI
utterances.text: In 1999 and now also I live together with my parents in the same house but with different floors -- on different floors.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Were your parents living in the same house with you in March 1999?

utterances.speaker: EDISON ZATRIQI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And now tell me, please, if I recall well, you've completed high school; correct?

utterances.speaker: EDISON ZATRIQI
utterances.text: Yes, I completed high school but also the Faculty of Economics in Prishtina.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. When did you graduate, what year?

utterances.speaker: EDISON ZATRIQI
utterances.text: Rather late I would say, sometime in 1988.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And when did you get employed?

utterances.speaker: EDISON ZATRIQI
utterances.text: For the first time I was employed in Prishtina temporarily. I worked there for a year in the then-statistical institute until 1981.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And then?

utterances.speaker: EDISON ZATRIQI
utterances.text: Then I returned to Peje and started working in the Ljubljana bank in 1985.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you serve in the army?

utterances.speaker: EDISON ZATRIQI
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Could you tell me when and where?

utterances.speaker: EDISON ZATRIQI
utterances.text: I served in the army in Skopje in 1982 until February 1983.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And what was your military speciality?

utterances.speaker: EDISON ZATRIQI
utterances.text: I was working in the communications sector, then they needed a driver, and I was the only one who had a licence; so I was transferred to that -- I became a driver, actually, and I did a driving course in Kurqoll [phoen].

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Were you a member of a political party after 1999 [as interpreted] -- correction in the transcript, please, not 1999 but 1990.

utterances.speaker: EDISON ZATRIQI
utterances.text: Yes, I was until 1989, I think, member of the then-communist party of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And after 1990, when the multi-party system was introduced ... ?

utterances.speaker: EDISON ZATRIQI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Zatriqi, do you recall making a statement -- giving a statement on the 20th of June, 2001, to an investigator of the ICTY?

utterances.speaker: EDISON ZATRIQI
utterances.text: Yes, I recall it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Was that the first statement that you provided to the investigator of the Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: EDISON ZATRIQI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it fair to say that this statement was read back to you in the Albanian language?

utterances.speaker: EDISON ZATRIQI
utterances.text: Yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And it is also stated here that you have given your statement to the best of your knowledge and abilities and recollections; correct?

utterances.speaker: EDISON ZATRIQI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Zatriqi, could you please tell me, did you -- were you ever brought to a court of law? Were you ever tried in a -- in criminal proceedings?

utterances.speaker: EDISON ZATRIQI
utterances.text: Can you make the question clearer? What period are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: I did mention that but probably it wasn't recorded in the transcript. Up to 1990 [as interpreted], had you ever been tried?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Correction, please, not up to 1990 but in 1990. I apologise. I still see the same year. So I will repeat my question.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Up until 1999, had you ever been tried in a court of law?

utterances.speaker: EDISON ZATRIQI
utterances.text: Yes, I was tried in a court of law prior to 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you tell us when and on what grounds?

utterances.speaker: EDISON ZATRIQI
utterances.text: The trial took place at the end of 1998 and the subject was described as smuggling of medicinal means, medicaments.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Djurdjic, that appears to be the time now. We must adjourn, and we continue tomorrow. I'm afraid, sir, we must adjourn now, and we continue with the evidence tomorrow. The court officer will give you explanations and the Victims and Witnesses Unit. We would be grateful if you could return tomorrow to complete your evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 28th day of April, 2009, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.46 p.m.,
